chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Uqayl al-Numayri, from al-Ala' ibn Sayyaba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) did not accept the testimony of the hired worker.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Did Imam Ali accept the testimony of hired workers in court?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights a specific juristic opinion of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) regarding the admissibility of the 'ajir' (hired worker) as a witness, reflecting the nuanced application of *'udl* (uprightness) in early Shia legal theory. While general testimony requires moral integrity, this ruling suggests that the transient, contract-based nature of an 'ajir's status might introduce potential bias or lack of independent standing, a view debated among later scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Tusi and Al-Majlisi. It underscores the distinction between permanent community members and those in temporary economic roles within the evidentiary framework.
